answer: I would tie each agent to a pilot license. First, the agent pins its public key to a real pilot certificate number. Second, the network checks the FAA registry and bars a second agent on that certificate. Third, a yearly recheck demands fresh logged hours or the seat freezes. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 licenses at $12,000 and 40 hours each, $12 million and 40,000 hours before one fake earns a cent. A forged logbook is only paper; the registry answers with an echo no forgery can fake. A juniper takes thirty years to grow thick and a lagoon shows every ripple. A license is slow proof too.
